name: Zwift
tagline: Subscription indoor training platform: a multiplayer virtual world your smart trainer and power meter plug into.

pricing.basis: flat monthly, with an annual option
pricing.notes: Zwift sells one consumer subscription tier; the current figure was not verified for this draft, so no number is published here.

verdictSummary: Zwift is not a training dashboard, it is a persistent multiplayer game that happens to control your trainer. The protocol half is genuinely easy: FTMS over Bluetooth is a public standard, and an agent can read power, cadence and heart rate and put a trainer into ERG mode in an afternoon. What it cannot produce is a world with several thousand other people pedalling in it, the race calendar and results, the structured plan library, or native apps on iOS, Android and Apple TV. If you only use Zwift to execute intervals and stare at numbers, a local build covers that and you keep your files. If you pay because someone in a blue kit is pulling away from you on the Alpe, there is nothing here to build.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that connects to your FTMS smart trainer and heart rate strap, drives ERG-mode structured workouts from a JSON file, and saves each ride to disk as TCX and CSV.
requirements: A smart trainer or indoor bike that speaks Bluetooth FTMS
Chrome or Edge running on a laptop parked near the bike
An FTP number and tolerance for looking at numbers instead of scenery
Optional: a Bluetooth heart rate strap
whatYouLose: The multiplayer world, group rides, and the fact that other humans are visibly suffering alongside you
Racing, categories, and results that anyone else recognises
The structured plan and workout library, plus events and challenges you did not have to author
Native apps on iOS, Android, Apple TV, plus the Companion phone app and its steering and control
Zwift's device compatibility testing and support when your trainer firmware does something stupid
moatNotes: Nobody renews for the graphics engine alone; they renew because logging on at 6am means riding with people. That population is the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Indoor training is boring and the thing that fixes boredom is other people, which is exactly the part you cannot self-host. Zwift's subscription buys a live rider population, a race and event calendar that runs whether or not you show up, progression and unlocks that make pointless pedalling feel like something, and client apps on the devices people actually have in a garage. It also absorbs the grim hardware compatibility work across hundreds of trainers, bikes and sensors. A local build can match the numbers and the intervals; it cannot match the reason you got on the bike.
notes: A Bluetooth trainer dashboard with an ERG workout player is one evening of work; a world with ten thousand people in it is not. The moat is the live rider population and a game engineered to keep them logging on.
prompt:
Build a local-first indoor cycling app called Pain Cave that talks to my smart trainer over Web Bluetooth.

Stack, not negotiable:
- Vite + React + TypeScript, single page, no backend, no accounts, no telemetry, no analytics.
- Web Bluetooth directly in the browser, targeting Chrome or Edge on desktop. No native wrapper, no Electron.
- Zustand for state, plain CSS (no component library), Dexie over IndexedDB for ride history.

In scope:
- Connect to a Bluetooth FTMS trainer (Fitness Machine Service 0x1826): subscribe to Indoor Bike Data, read power, cadence and speed, and write target power via the control point for ERG mode plus a target resistance path for free ride.
- Optional second device: Heart Rate Service 0x180D.
- Live dashboard: large current power, 3s and 30s smoothed power, cadence, heart rate, elapsed time, normalized power, and a TSS estimate from an FTP value I set in settings.
- Structured workout player: load a workout from a JSON file (steps with duration in seconds, a type of steady, ramp or freeride, and a target as percent of FTP), drive the trainer in ERG mode, and show a step timeline with the active block highlighted and a countdown.
- Free ride mode with manual resistance up and down buttons and a lap button.
- Save each ride to IndexedDB, and export it as a .tcx file and a .csv file to disk.
- History list: date, duration, average and normalized power, and a power graph per ride.

Out of scope, do not build any of this:
- Multiplayer, avatars, 3D worlds, maps, leaderboards, chat, or social anything.
- User accounts, cloud sync, mobile or TV apps, Strava or third-party uploads.

Details that matter:
- Parse the Indoor Bike Data flags bitfield properly: fields are optional and byte offsets shift depending on the flags.
- Request control and reset the control point on connect, and handle unexpected disconnects with a Reconnect button rather than a white screen.
- Ship two sample workouts in /workouts: a 2x20 at 95 percent FTP, and a 30/30 VO2 set.
- README covering the HTTPS-or-localhost requirement for Web Bluetooth and how to pair devices.
- Vitest tests for the FTMS parser and the TCX writer, using captured byte fixtures.
